headline: Cambri gets five touchdowns from Drake Maye and loses anyway, which is officially her superpower
dek: Puka Nacua caught seventeen passes for Cambri and it bought her exactly nothing. Kyra is 5-0 after a 64.64-point blowout of Amie. Maddie's quarterback finished below zero, which takes commitment. And Tara beat this year's presumptive Toilet Bowl champion by 7.84, thanks to the same Christian Watson she kept benching.

matchups.1-7: Samantha left just 2.4 points on her bench, the tightest in the league. Marlee left George Pickens on hers for 28 points and lost by 20.98. Marlee didn't lose to Samantha. She lost to a man she personally chose to sit, and she should be asked to explain herself.
matchups.2-6: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.7 and Jaylen Warren scored 36.8 out of Kyra's backfield. Amie made the smart move, grabbing Jayden Daniels off waivers and starting him over a scoreless Patrick Mahomes, and still lost by 64.64. When your best move of the week gets you blown out, the problem is the opponent, and the opponent is Kyra.
matchups.3-5: Bucky Irving ran for 165 yards and scored twice, and Maya won by 49.6. She also benched Mike Evans (26.3) for Omarion Hampton (4.9) in the flex, the second week in a row Evans has outscored her starter from the bench. This is no longer a mistake, it's a hobby. Maddie's Tyler Shough, meanwhile, finished at −0.16 points.
matchups.4-8: Tara won the closest game of the week by 7.84, and Christian Watson, who haunted her bench in Weeks 1 and 3, finally showed up: two touchdowns, 32.3 points. Cambri got huge games from both her quarterback and her top receiver and still lost, this time to Tara.

game_balls.title: Five and oh, playing for second
game_balls.text: Kyra scored 170.3 behind Jahmyr Gibbs (37.7, two touchdowns, 151 rushing yards) and Jaylen Warren (36.8 from the flex). She's the last unbeaten team in the league, so the rest of you are now playing for second.

game_balls.title: Nothing left on the table
game_balls.text: Samantha left 2.4 points on her bench, the tightest in the league. Josh Allen gave her 30.5 points against a 19.9 projection, and the Texans D/ST she picked up off free agency the same week added 15 more. Every move worked, and the rest of us would like to see the process, preferably in writing.

game_balls.title: Bucky remembers
game_balls.text: Maya benched Bucky Irving in Week 1. This week he ran for 165 yards and scored twice and she won by 49.6. Enjoy this one, Maya, because you're back in the flags section, and this time it's a pattern.

flags.title: George Pickens, seated
flags.text: George Pickens scored 28 on Marlee's bench and she lost by 20.98. Swap him in for Michael Wilson's 7.28 and she still loses, by 0.26. Close enough to taste it, not close enough to matter, and the league still has questions about why Wilson started over him.

flags.title: The person writing this recap did it again
flags.text: Maya played Omarion Hampton (4.9) in the flex and left Mike Evans (26.3) on the bench, for the second week in a row. She won by 49.6, so the damage was zero. But when the author of the recap makes the same mistake twice, the recap has a conflict of interest and the commissioner has no choice but to call it out.

tough_breaks.title: Five touchdowns, still a loss
tough_breaks.text: Drake Maye accounted for five touchdowns and Puka Nacua caught seventeen passes. Cambri still lost to Tara by 7.84. If losing is her superpower, it's the only one that comes with a fully stacked offense.

tough_breaks.title: Right call, wrong week
tough_breaks.text: Amie's waiver move looked perfect: Jayden Daniels in, a scoreless Patrick Mahomes out. She still lost by 64.64. Kyra's backfield did not care about her process.

tough_breaks.title: Below zero
tough_breaks.text: Tyler Shough finished at −0.16 points, a negative score for a quarterback. It's a rare achievement, and nobody should try to repeat it.

glossary.definition: Dropping the ball and having the other team recover it, which costs two points on top of whatever was already earned, as it did for both Brock Bowers and Mark Andrews this week.
A bonus play worth two points instead of one, run after a touchdown instead of kicking the extra point. Josh Allen converted one for Samantha this week, on top of his two touchdowns.
The consolation contest for the worst teams. Winning it is not an honor, and the exact rules vary by league.
